name: Cursor Pro+

reset.rule: Resets on your monthly billing date.
stipulations: Covers Grok 4.7, Grok 4.6, Grok 4.5 and Composer 2.5.
Auto draws from this pool unless it routes to a third-party model.
Cursor's usage API reports the exact cycle end.

meters.label: Third-party models pool
meters.hint: Claude, GPT, Gemini at API price

reset.rule: Resets on your monthly billing date.
stipulations: Each request is charged at that model's API list price.
Auto draws from this pool when it routes to a third-party model.
A subagent that names a third-party model draws from this pool, even when the parent chat uses Auto, Grok or Composer.
Cursor sometimes adds bonus usage on top of the included amount.

overage: On-demand usage bills monthly in arrears at API rates, up to the spend limit set at cursor.com/dashboard/spending. It's off by default; quota-board shows whether yours is on.

how: Two monthly pools that reset with your billing cycle: Cursor's own models, and third-party models at API price.
Includes Bugbot, Cloud Agents, Automations, Origin and the SDK.
ext: Third-party models (Claude, GPT, Gemini) are included through the third-party pool at API list price, with no markup.
quirks: Cursor Pro+ is no longer sold. Your plan, price and features continue until you switch or cancel.

Switching to a new plan is permanent and Support can't reverse it. You lose the included third-party pool, on-demand billing and the monthly reset. Third-party models then cost API price from the first request, paid from prepaid credit. The comparable new plan is Super ($100).
If you switch, any unbilled on-demand usage is invoiced first, the old plan is refunded pro rata, and a new billing cycle starts that day.
Cursor doesn't publish Pro+'s pool sizes, only that they are larger than Pro's. Earlier pricing put them at 3x Pro (third-party report, unconfirmed).
Upgrades between Pro, Pro+ and Ultra apply at once. Downgrades apply at the end of the billing period.
Bugbot bills from included usage first, then from on-demand usage if it's on.
Billing settings may show limited-time offers for switching. Cursor doesn't publish their terms.
